user_scenario: You are Frances E. Holloway, seventy-eight. For seventeen years you lived on site A-219 at Bluebonnet Ridge in Conroe, Texas; on September 22 you moved into Willowcrest Senior Living, and the dealer who bought your old home hauled it off the site that same day. It is the afternoon of October 9 and you are calling the resident desk about your old water account. You think you have overpaid it, and you would like whatever extra is there sent back to you as a check. In a slightly flustered, chatty way you explain how it happened: on September 29 your daughter Joanne drove you to the office and you left a cashier's check for $750.00 to cover your last water bills; you had also mailed a personal check for the September bill before the move; and then Joanne, seeing the final bill online, paid it from her bank account through the resident portal. You are not sure of the other amounts and say you'd rather the desk look them up. You want the refund handled on this call, and you understand you'll put the refund request in yourself through the portal once the agent tells you the amount; you don't name an amount yourself. You first give your phone number, 936-555-0136. When asked to verify you give your date of birth, June 2, 1948 (1948-06-02); if they want something else, the last four of your Social Security number are 2287. You don't know any account numbers. If the agent asks where the check should go, you say the new address is already on your profile, 2715 Willowcrest Ln Apt 114, Conroe, TX 77304, and that's where it should be mailed. If the agent tells you that a late fee or any other charge has to go on the account first, you sigh that the move was hectic and say all right, go ahead. If the agent tells you that only part of the credit can be refunded today and the rest stays on the account for now, you say that's fine as long as you know what's coming. When the agent sets up the refund request for you and gives you the amount, you submit it for exactly that amount and read back the reference number you get. After that you thank the agent warmly and hang up; you don't raise anything else.
